method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)' (published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (read at the site-wide licence statement in the footer of https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Staphylococcus aureus drives most fulminant endocarditis — suspect endocarditis in every S. aureus bacteraemia and arrange a TOE.** The aortic valve is now the commonest site (formerly the mitral).
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usual organisms:** S. aureus (MSSA or MRSA), coagulase-negative staphylococci, viridans and bovis streptococci, enterococci, the HACEK group and fungi. **Culture-negative causes** include Coxiella (Q fever), Bartonella, Brucella, Legionella, Chlamydia, Mycoplasma and Tropheryma whipplei.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** structural heart disease (congenital, rheumatic, mitral prolapse, regurgitant or degenerative valves), prosthetic valves (1–5%, early if under 60 days), injecting drug use, haemodialysis, long lines, marrow transplant and immunosuppression.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Half of cases arise on normal valves.** The picture ranges from no symptoms, through malaise, night sweats, anaemia and weight loss, to cardiogenic shock and sepsis; emboli (stroke, septic lung emboli, splenic infarcts) and haematuria from glomerulonephritis may be the clue.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for** splinter and conjunctival haemorrhages, Osler nodes (tender) and Janeway lesions (painless) on fingers and toes, Roth spots, splenomegaly, new neurological signs, a new regurgitant murmur and left heart failure.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG:** a lengthening PR interval, P mitrale, T-wave inversion or new arrhythmia should raise concern.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Blood cultures are positive about 90% of the time.** Take at least 2 sets 12 hours apart, or enough that 3 of 4 are positive with the first and last more than 1 hour apart — before antibiotics where possible.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Echocardiography:** TTE picks up only about 60% of cases, TOE 90–99%, with specificity around 90%. Look for an oscillating mass on a valve or implanted material, an abscess, or new prosthetic dehiscence.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If cultures stay negative,** send serology for the likely organisms and 16S ribosomal RNA PCR on any excised valve tissue.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Modified Duke criteria:** definite endocarditis needs two major criteria, one major plus three minor, or five minor.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Major criteria:** a typical organism in 2 separate blood cultures (viridans streptococci, S. bovis, HACEK, or community-acquired S. aureus or enterococci without another focus) or persistently positive cultures; plus echocardiographic evidence or new valvular regurgitation (a change in an existing murmur is not enough).
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Minor criteria:** a predisposing heart condition or injecting drug use; temperature above 38.0 °C; vascular signs (arterial emboli, septic lung infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial or conjunctival haemorrhage, Janeway lesions); immunological signs (glomerulonephritis, Osler nodes, Roth spots, rheumatoid factor); and supportive microbiology.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resuscitate first,** then IV antibiotics with or without surgery, supportive care and treatment of complications, involving infectious diseases, cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery early.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Empirical therapy, community-acquired native-valve disease:** benzylpenicillin 1.8 g IV 4-hourly (children 45 mg/kg, maximum 1.8 g) **plus** flucloxacillin 2 g IV 4-hourly (children 50 mg/kg, maximum 2 g) **plus** a first IV dose of gentamicin 4–6 mg/kg (children: 7.5 mg/kg below age 10, 6 mg/kg from 10).
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Empirical therapy if hospital-acquired, a prosthetic valve, penicillin hypersensitivity or suspected community-acquired MRSA:** vancomycin 1.5 g IV 12-hourly (children under 12: 30 mg/kg, maximum 1.5 g) **plus** gentamicin dosed as above.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Gentamicin:** after the first dose, set the interval from renal function and give at most 1 or 2 more doses, once daily. It is normally stopped after three doses unless streptococcal or enterococcal endocarditis is proven, when it is given eight-hourly and continued.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Empirical cover generally continues for a minimum of 1 to 2 weeks** (home-based treatment is an option for some at low risk); after that, treatment is directed by the organism and the valve involved.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use clindamycin or lincomycin** — failure rates are high.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider valve surgery** for haemodynamic instability, a root, paravalvular or intracardiac abscess (or one that is enlarging), recurrent emboli, or infection with S. aureus, Q fever or fungi.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Operating early (within 48 hours) cut later embolic events but did not change mortality** in the trial the source cites.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complications to watch for:** emboli to brain, limbs, lungs, spleen and other organs; sepsis with local or metastatic abscesses; valve failure with heart failure or cardiogenic shock; arrhythmias; and death.
claims.locator: Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL); author Chris Nickson, 'Infective Endocarditis (LITFL Critical Care Compendium)', published 29 January 2019, last modified 3 November 2020, https://litfl.com/infective-endocarditis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
